expectations.text: Map: reality is the ultimate update
Map: consider the cartographer
Map: maps can influence territories (e.g., Jane Jacobs / city planners)
Circle: built/maintained with curiosity (desire to learn), monitoring track record, and feedback
Outside circle: learn the basics, talk to someone with strong competence, use broad mental models
expectations.evidence: Learn basics, ask expert, broad models

expectations.text: Uses the Lifer vs Stranger illustration or mentions Korzybski
Probabilistic thinking has three parts: Bayesian thinking, fat-tailed curves, asymmetries
Explains asymmetries as metaprobability / estimates being over-optimistic (e.g., investors' 20-40% forecasts)
Inversion: two approaches (assume true/false and see what else must be true; think about what to avoid)
Mentions Jacobi 'invert, always invert'
Gives a book example of inversion (Hippasus sqrt 2, Bernays/Lucky Strike, or Marie Van Brittan Brown CCTV)
Includes Kurt Lewin's force field analysis steps
Names the book's nine models (map/territory, circle of competence, first principles, thought experiment, second-order, probabilistic, inversion, Occam's razor, Hanlon's razor)
Applies first principles with Socratic questioning and/or Five Whys
Applies second-order thinking (consequences of consequences) to the decision
Applies inversion (what would make it fail / what to avoid)
Applies probabilistic thinking with base rates/Bayesian updating
Applies circle of competence with the operate-outside advice (learn basics, consult experts)
